name: Beam

modes.label: Sandbox (CPU, Performance tier, default for new accounts), per-ms per vCPU + GiB
modes.note: Pricing page 2026-11-08, Sandboxes: $0.05/hr per vCPU + $0.01/hr per GiB, "Billed by the millisecond while running"; example 2 vCPU / 8 GiB on Performance = $0.18/hr. Priced per vCPU (the old per-core = 2 vCPU sheet, $0.0675/vCPU-h + $0.02304/GiB-h, is gone). Performance = "No CPU sharing, not preemptible"; "New accounts default to Performance, and workloads opt into Shared or Spot" (https://docs.beam.cloud/v2/resources/pricing-and-billing.md). Python Sandbox default lifetime 600 s; keep_warm_seconds is a TTL, -1 = terminate explicitly (https://docs.beam.cloud/v2/sandbox/configuration.md): the TTL tail bills, so auto_stop_idle = false. Default sandbox runtime is a container; US by default.
modes.perf_source: ComputeSDK (each provider at its SDK default size and runtime): burst 534 ms median at 100 at once, 100% succeeded (2026-11-06); DAX clone + install + typecheck 99.88 s (2026-11-06, one run; sandbox saw 64 CPUs / 16 GiB x86); one-at-a-time start 105 ms (sequential TTI, latest published run 2026-08-07 or older). https://github.com/computesdk/benchmarks/tree/main/results

modes.label: Sandbox (CPU, Shared tier: shared vCPUs, up to 8 vCPU / 16 GiB)
modes.note: Pricing page 2026-11-08: Shared $0.011/vCPU-hour + $0.0055/GiB-hour, "Shared vCPUs, not preemptible", up to 8 vCPU / 16 GiB; tiers are chosen "per workload for CPU functions, sandboxes and VMs". Opt in with Sandbox(cpu_tier="shared", cpu=2, memory="2Gi") (beam-client >= 0.2.236) (https://docs.beam.cloud/v2/sandbox/configuration.md). Tiered VM-backed sandboxes need at least 1 vCPU / 1 GiB. CPU is shared with other tenants, so per-vCPU speed can be lower than Performance.

modes.label: Sandbox (CPU, Spot tier: interruptible with 30 s notice)
modes.note: Pricing page 2026-11-08: Spot $0.0063/vCPU-hour + $0.00135/GiB-hour, "May be interrupted". Docs: Spot "may be interrupted with 30 seconds' notice"; "Spot sandboxes terminate when reclaimed. Persistent mounts survive, but process state and temporary files do not." (https://docs.beam.cloud/v2/sandbox/configuration.md).

modes.label: Sandbox with GPU (rate not published)
modes.note: Sandbox GPU rates are not published (pricing page 2026-11-08 lists serverless GPU and GPU machines only), so gpu prices are null and this regime is unpriced. Published serverless rates for reference: RTX 4090 $0.69/h, RTX 5090 $1.09/h, plus CPU attached to a GPU $0.18972/vCPU-h and $0.0198/GiB-h on every tier. Developer: 5 concurrent GPUs; Team: 50.

modes.label: Virtual machine (CPU microVM, Performance tier, persistent root, per-second while running)
modes.note: Pricing page 2026-11-08 (Virtual machines): Performance $0.06/hr for 1 vCPU / 1 GiB ($0.05/vCPU-h + $0.01/GiB-h), "Billed per second while running. No compute charges while stopped." 4 vCPU / 8 GiB = $0.28/h on Performance, the default tier for new accounts (https://docs.beam.cloud/v2/vm/configuration.md). Root disk default 50 GiB, max 100 GiB. Stop keeps the disk and drops RAM; pause keeps RAM and processes. Idle TTL and auto-resume are opt-in (off by default). Browser desktop (Chrome on x86-64) with SDK screenshot/click/type/record (https://docs.beam.cloud/v2/vm/desktop.md). Persistent public IPv6 with published TCP ports, token-protected URLs; no inbound IPv4 listed (https://docs.beam.cloud/v2/vm/networking.md). CPU only ("VMs are persistent Linux machines without GPUs").
modes.perf_source: No benchmark of Beam VMs yet; ComputeSDK numbers are for the container sandbox.

modes.label: Virtual machine (Shared tier: shared vCPUs, up to 8 vCPU / 16 GiB)
modes.note: Pricing page 2026-11-08: Shared $0.011/vCPU-hour + $0.0055/GiB-hour, "Shared vCPUs, not preemptible", up to 8 vCPU / 16 GiB. 4 vCPU / 8 GiB = $0.088/h. Same VM features as the Performance VM (https://docs.beam.cloud/v2/vm/configuration.md). CPU is shared with other tenants.

modes.label: Virtual machine (Spot tier: interruptible, restart by hand)
modes.note: Pricing page 2026-11-08: Spot $0.0063/vCPU-hour + $0.00135/GiB-hour, "May be interrupted. Restart preempted VMs manually." 4 vCPU / 8 GiB = $0.036/h. Docs: "A preempted Spot VM gets a 30-second graceful shutdown window." "Its disk and URLs remain, but memory is lost." (https://docs.beam.cloud/v2/vm/configuration.md).

modes.label: Serverless function / pod (not a sandbox), per-ms per vCPU + GiB
modes.note: Pricing page 2026-11-08, Serverless CPU-only: $0.05/hr per vCPU + $0.01/hr per GiB, "Billed by the millisecond while code runs" (the old 1/3-of-sandbox rate is gone). Billed incl. on_start and keep_warm_seconds (defaults: endpoints 180 s, task queues 10 s, pods 600 s). Functions, endpoints and pods get plaintext env secrets, not brokered placeholders. No sandbox exec/fs/snapshot API.

perf_source: Several runtimes (sandbox, GPU sandbox, serverless containers, GPU machines): perf is on the CPU sandbox mode only.

knobs.label: keep_warm idle tail (x session hours)
knobs.why: Beam bills a sandbox until terminate() or until its keep_warm_seconds TTL expires. The SDK default TTL is 600 s (10 min) when keep_warm_seconds is not set, so a sandbox that is never terminate()d bills a 10-minute idle tail; -1 never expires; docs examples use 30 min-2 h. Factor = (session + TTL) / session; 1 = explicit terminate().

caveats: CPU is priced per vCPU on three tiers (pricing page 2026-11-08): Spot $0.0063/vCPU-h + $0.00135/GiB-h (interruptible, 30 s notice), Shared $0.011 + $0.0055 (shared vCPUs, max 8 vCPU / 16 GiB), Performance $0.05 + $0.01 (dedicated). New accounts default to Performance. The same tier rates apply to sandboxes and VMs.

Dated price change: the 2026-09-28 sheet priced sandboxes per physical core (= 2 vCPU) at $0.0675/vCPU-h + $0.02304/GiB-h, and serverless at 1/3 of that. The 2026-11-08 sheet is per vCPU, and serverless CPU equals the sandbox Performance rate.
Developer plan: $20/month with $20 of monthly credit (pricing page 2026-11-08). The 2026-09-28 sheet had a $0 Developer plan.
Plan limits count concurrent vCPUs across VMs, sandboxes and serverless apps (30 Developer, 1,000 Team), not containers. Four 8-vCPU sandboxes need Team.
Idle keep_warm TTL tail is billed at full rate until expiry (Python Sandbox default lifetime 600 s; -1 never expires).

Storage (volumes, snapshots, VM disks) is not billed yet; the planned rate is $0.0001/GB-hour with no free allowance (https://docs.beam.cloud/v2/resources/pricing-and-billing.md). Egress is free on every plan.
Sandbox GPU pricing is not published; the sandbox-gpu regime is left unpriced (gpu rates null). On-demand GPU machine prices conflict between pricing page and docs GPU page (pricing page used).

Isolation: default sandboxes are containers (Beam's blog says gVisor; CLI prompt shows runc). VMs and VM-backed sandboxes run in a CPU microVM. beam shell gives a root prompt, so root=true. No systemd in container sandboxes (Beam VMs have systemd).

Workloads run in the US "unless you choose a specific region" (security page); no region list is published, so every mode stays US-only and eu_data_residency is unclear. BYOC runs in your own AWS/GCP/Azure account and region.
BYOC fee is per vCPU and excludes the cloud VM bill. Self-hosted beta9 (AGPL) has no Beam fee.
BYOC regime is a management fee only: add your own cloud bill (compute, storage, egress from AWS/GCP/Azure).

Sandbox root-filesystem size is not published. Sandbox files survive a stop through create_image_from_filesystem() (an image id for the next sandbox) or an attached Volume / DurableDisk; persist_scope = snapshot.

Secrets in sandboxes and VMs are brokered: "the guest receives a stable beam_secret_... placeholder" and Beam substitutes the real value "only in HTTPS request headers sent to approved hosts" (https://docs.beam.cloud/v2/vm/secrets.md). Functions, endpoints, pods and image builds get plaintext env values.
Desktop, browser and computer-use SDK are documented for Beam VMs only (vm modes), not for sandboxes. Desktop is on by default from the CLI for fresh images; SDK callers set desktop=True.

Beam VM inbound: token-protected URLs and published TCP ports on a persistent public IPv6 address; no inbound IPv4 is listed, so IPv4-only clients cannot reach a raw TCP port. Sandbox URLs are public HTTPS with no built-in auth.
Spot modes: Spot sandboxes terminate when reclaimed (mounts survive, process state does not); Spot VMs keep disk and URLs but lose memory and must be restarted by hand.

fleet.tiers: Developer ($20/month incl. $20 credit): 30 concurrent vCPUs and 5 concurrent GPUs; Team ($89/month): 1,000 vCPUs and 50 GPUs; Growth: custom limits via contact.
fleet.notes: "Concurrent vCPUs is the total CPU running at once across VMs, sandboxes, and serverless apps, not a count of containers." (pricing page). No quota-increase turnaround stated.

audit_2026_09_29.source: checked against the provider's live pricing and docs pages

snapshot_auto.note: Sandboxes terminate when keep_warm_seconds expires; no pause/sleep with state capture is documented, snapshots are explicit SDK calls. Only exception: attached DurableDisks are snapshotted to object storage on container stop ('Beam snapshots a disk to object storage each time the container using it stops', https://docs.beam.cloud/v2/data/durable-disks.md). That is disk-only persistence of an extra attached disk, not the sandbox's state, so not counted here.

snapshot_on_demand.quote: You can use Snapshots as a base image for any other abstraction or Sandbox on Beam, using `Image.from_id`
snapshot_on_demand.note: create_image_from_filesystem() returns an image id; snapshot_memory() "captures the sandbox's process state and filesystem on supported runtimes" (runtimes not listed). The docs do not mention GPU state. Storage is not billed yet (planned $0.0001/GB-hour). Beam VMs also fork and take filesystem restore points.

harness_api.quote: A sandboxed container for running Python code or arbitrary processes.
harness_api.note: The Sandbox SDK exposes only process exec/run_code, filesystem, ports, snapshots, network, Docker. No API to start/stream/resume Claude Code/Codex/etc. Beam's 'agents' docs are a petri-net agent framework, and the new MCP server (beta9 PR #1920/#1942) lets an outside agent drive Beam (deploy, pods, secrets), not a harness running inside a sandbox. 'Managed agents' in commits are Beam's worker-machine agents.

egress_allowlist.quote: Allowlists accept up to 64 entries, including bare IPv4/IPv6 addresses and CIDRs.
egress_allowlist.note: block_network or an allow list of up to 64 hostnames, wildcard domains (*.example.com, apex excluded), IPs or CIDRs. Hostname rules match TLS SNI on 443 or HTTP Host on 80; other TCP ports need IP/CIDR rules. Changes apply to a running sandbox or VM without restart.

egress_http_rules.quote: Must use proper CIDR notation (e.g., "8.8.8.8/32" for a single IP, "10.0.0.0/8" for a range)
egress_http_rules.note: Hostname rules match only SNI/Host; nothing at HTTP method/path/header level is documented.

ingress_rules.quote: Exposed sandbox URLs are public. Add authentication inside the application before exposing sensitive data or operations.
ingress_rules.note: Sandboxes: exposed URLs are public; the docs say to add authentication inside the application. Beam VMs (vm modes) have token-protected URLs (--protected-port; terminal and desktop protected; browser links time-limited 1-3600 s) (https://docs.beam.cloud/v2/vm/networking.md). Not counted at card level because the default sandbox has no inbound auth.

secret_proxy.quote: the worker substitutes the real value only in HTTPS request headers sent to approved hosts
secret_proxy.note: Applies to sandbox and VM runtime bindings: the guest sees a beam_secret_... placeholder. Limit: substitution happens only in HTTPS headers, not in query strings or bodies. Ordinary containers, pods, functions, endpoints, task queues and image builds get plaintext env values. Sandbox config page: runtime secrets "receive placeholders, substituted only in HTTPS headers to approved hosts".

volume_attach.quote: Mount fast storage volumes to persist files between sessions
volume_attach.note: Volumes, CloudBucket (your S3-compatible bucket) and DurableDisk attach to a Sandbox. Storage is not billed yet; planned $0.0001/GB-hour (https://docs.beam.cloud/v2/resources/pricing-and-billing.md).

volume_shared.quote: If several containers need to read and write the same files at the same time, use a [Volume](/v2/data/volume) instead. Volumes are shared, distributed storage.
volume_shared.note: Volumes are read-write shared across containers/sandboxes (writes visible to others within ~60 s); CloudBuckets also shared. DurableDisks: one writer at a time, any number of read-only mounts.

nested_virt.quote: Workloads run in isolated containers. The effective user depends on the image and runtime configuration; a custom image is not guaranteed to run as a non-root user.
nested_virt.note: Default sandboxes are containers. No /dev/kvm or nested-virtualization capability is documented for sandboxes, VM-backed sandboxes or Beam VMs (VM overview, configuration and CLI pages, 2026-11-08).

anti_bot.quote: Sandboxes are ultra-fast, Python-native environments for running any workload - with GPUs, networking, and persistent storage - in seconds.
anti_bot.note: Beam VMs have a Chrome desktop, but no stealth or fingerprint-evasion feature is documented.

captcha_solving.quote: Sandboxes are ultra-fast, Python-native environments for running any workload - with GPUs, networking, and persistent storage - in seconds.
captcha_solving.note: No CAPTCHA-solving feature is documented for sandboxes or the VM desktop.

egress_ip_type.quote: Pods are served in a static IP range, making it possible to whitelist the Beam IP range from the client.
egress_ip_type.note: Outbound traffic comes from AWS/GCP datacenter ranges (security page: infrastructure on AWS/GCP). Documented explicitly as a fixed/static IP range for Pods (contact Beam for the range); Sandbox docs don't repeat this, but sandboxes share the same network egress path, so a fixed datacenter range is the best-supported answer rather than plain rotating datacenter IPs.

fork_running.quote: You can also create a memory snapshot of a running Sandbox, which will capture the state of the sandbox's memory - including all running processes and exposed ports.
fork_running.note: The docs example calls sandbox.snapshot_memory() on a sandbox that is still running (a server process is executing and a port is exposed) and only calls terminate() afterward; the snapshot is not preceded by stopping the sandbox. The resulting snapshot can be used via create_from_memory_snapshot() to clone a new sandbox with processes/state intact, i.e. forking a running machine without stopping it.

wake_on_request.note: For the Sandbox product (this card's primary mode), a sandbox that hits its keep_warm_seconds TTL (or is terminate()d) is gone; there is no documented mechanism for an external request to automatically wake/recreate a terminated sandbox with its prior state (memory snapshots must be explicitly restored via create_from_memory_snapshot()). This matches the card's own mode-level features (auto_stop_idle sandbox modes: wake_on_request=false). Beam's separate serverless containers (Endpoints/pods, an alt/paas mode) do scale from zero on an incoming request (wake_on_request=true there), but that is a different product surface than the Sandbox.

live_resize.note: The SandboxInstance API only exposes expose_port(), list_urls(), update_network_permissions(), update_ttl(), terminate(), create_image_from_filesystem(), snapshot_memory() -- no update_cpu/update_memory/resize method. The configuration docs tell users to create a new, bigger sandbox instead of resizing ('If you need more power, create a new sandbox'), confirming CPU/RAM cannot be changed on a running sandbox.

own_agent_api.quote: Beam is launching a new type of agent framework that is stateful and has concurrency built-in.
own_agent_api.note: Beam's "agents" page is a framework to build your own agents; the VM desktop SDK drives the desktop but is not a Beam-run agent. Beam registers its MCP server with Claude Code, Codex and Cursor on your machine.

lang_node.quote:
Running a Node.js server
You can run arbitrary code on Beam. It doesn't need to be Python!
... sb = Sandbox(image=Image().from_registry("node:20")).create()
lang_node.note: Node.js is a documented first-class quickstart runtime for Sandboxes (via image), and Beam additionally ships a first-party TypeScript SDK (@beamcloud/beam-js) to drive Sandboxes/Pods/etc. from Node.js code.

guest_firewall.quote: Workloads run in isolated containers. The effective user depends on the image and runtime configuration; a custom image is not guaranteed to run as a non-root user.
guest_firewall.note: derived: the default sandbox is a gVisor container, not a full VM, so nftables/iptables inside the guest are not expected to work reliably even as root (root=true per the CLI shell transcript); outbound policy is enforced provider-side via allow_list/block_network (egress_allowlist). No page documents an in-guest firewall.

static_egress_ip.quote: Pods are served in a static IP range, making it possible to whitelist the Beam IP range from the client.
static_egress_ip.note: Documented for Pods only ("For the static IP range, send us a message in Slack"). The VM networking page says the VM's IPv6 "inbound address is not a fixed outbound source IP".

eu_data_residency.quote: Customer workloads run in the United States unless you choose a specific region or compute pool where the platform offers one.
eu_data_residency.note: doubtful "yes" could not be confirmed: the page allows a non-US region "where the platform offers one" but names no EU region, and no other docs/pricing page lists one. Self-hosting (beta9) or BYOC in your own EU cloud account would keep data in the EU, but that is not hosted EU residency. Left unclear.

root.quote: $ beam shell app.py:handler ... Welcome to Ubuntu 22.04.5 LTS (GNU/Linux 6.8.0-51-generic x86_64) root@runc:/mnt/code#
root.note: Beam's own CLI reference shows `beam shell` dropping you into a root@ prompt inside the container. The security page no longer promises a non-root user ("a custom image is not guaranteed to run as a non-root user", https://docs.beam.cloud/v2/security/security.md, 2026-10-14); the pricing FAQ still says "run in non-root containers". The CLI transcript is the concrete behavior, so root stays true.

pause_resume.quote: SandboxInstance.terminate() Terminate the container associated with this sandbox instance.
pause_resume.note: Sandboxes: only create()/terminate() plus a TTL; no pause call. Beam VMs (vm modes, pause_resume=true there): "Pausing keeps both [disk and RAM], and resuming restores them" (https://docs.beam.cloud/v2/resources/pricing-and-billing.md).

desktop.quote: The desktop has a browser and Terminal launcher.
desktop.note: Sandboxes: no desktop option is documented. Beam VMs (vm, vm-shared, vm-spot modes, desktop=true there) ship a browser Linux desktop; CLI creation includes it for fresh images, SDK callers set desktop=True.

browser.quote: On x86-64, the browser is Chrome; on ARM64 it is Firefox.
browser.note: Sandboxes: no bundled browser is documented (you can install one in the image). Beam VMs (vm modes, browser=true there) ship Chrome in the desktop.

computer_use.quote: Recording uses CPU encoding, with an FPS setting from 1 to 60.
computer_use.note: Beam VMs (vm modes, computer_use=true there) have a Python/JS SDK: screenshot(), click(), press() with X11 key names, and recording at 1-60 fps. Not documented for sandboxes.

public_ipv4.quote: When allocated, the VM's public IPv6 address appears in `beam vm new` and `beam vm get NAME`.
public_ipv4.note: Sandboxes reach the internet only through *.app.beam.cloud HTTPS URLs. Beam VMs get a persistent public IPv6 address, not IPv4.

agent_harnesses.note: No Claude Code/Codex template preinstalled in a sandbox or VM is documented. Beam registers its own MCP server with local Claude Code, Codex and Cursor sessions.

windows.quote: You can install Beam on Windows using Windows Subsystem for Linux (WSL).
windows.note: The only 'Windows' mention is running the local Beam CLI on a developer's Windows machine via WSL; the remote sandbox/container itself is Linux only (Ubuntu 22.04, per the CLI shell transcript). Not offered: outside the product's scope.

macos.quote: Beam lets you run functions, REST APIs, task queues, and sandboxes on CPUs and GPUs, end to end.
macos.note: Not offered: outside the product's scope. Beam runs customer workloads on AWS/GCP Linux infrastructure (docs.beam.cloud/v2/security/security.md: 'Beam runs on infrastructure provided by Amazon Web Services and Google Cloud'); no macOS machine type exists.

arm64.note: No architecture option appears in the sandbox, VM configuration or VM CLI docs (2026-11-08). The VM desktop page mentions Firefox "on ARM64", but no page says how to choose ARM64, so arm64 stays false.

sso.quote: single sign-on is not yet available
sso.note: Explicit first-party statement that SSO is not yet available. Confirms no.

max_session_h.note: No published hard cap on sandbox lifetime. keep_warm_seconds=-1 lets a sandbox run until you explicitly terminate() it ('Use manual termination for: Long-running training jobs, Collaborative development sessions, When you need to pause and resume work'). Docs/pricing/FAQ pages re-checked 2026-09-30 have no mention of a maximum session duration or forced eviction time, consistent with the card's own caveat 'Max sandbox size and max lifetime unpublished.' Treated as no limit rather than null since the platform explicitly supports indefinite manual-only termination.

usage_api.quote: Metrics endpoints (GET /metrics/{ws}/stub-timeseries, workspace-timeseries, pool-timeseries) return resource time series (CPU, memory, GPU, network) but not billable usage units or costs. Billing is visible in the dashboard only; no programmatic billing/cost API is documented.
usage_api.note: granularity: none; cost: no; Beam exposes metrics for monitoring (CPU/memory/GPU/network per container) via REST API and logs/task status endpoints, but no dedicated billing usage API that returns billable quantities (CPU-hours, RAM-hours, GPU-hours) or cost per sandbox/tag/project. Usage is only accessible through the account dashboard.

raw_tcp_inbound.quote: Published TCP ports use the same guest port number.
raw_tcp_inbound.note: Sandboxes: exposed ports are SSL-terminated HTTPS URLs only. Beam VMs (vm modes, raw_tcp_inbound=true there) publish TCP ports on a persistent public IPv6 address that survives stop/start and pause/resume; no inbound IPv4 and no inbound UDP are documented.

auto_stop_idle.quote: `keep_warm_seconds` is the sandbox's TTL, not an idle timeout that every command automatically resets.
auto_stop_idle.note: Sandbox TTL is not an idle timer. Beam VMs (vm modes) have an opt-in idle sleep (`--ttl SECONDS`, off by default) and opt-in auto-resume on access.

regions.quote: Customer workloads run in the United States unless you choose a specific region
regions.note: The security page allows choosing a region but names none; the pricing, sandbox and VM pages list no region (2026-11-08). Modes stay US-only. BYOC runs in your own cloud account and region.

persist_scope.how: call create_image_from_filesystem() before the sandbox ends and start the next sandbox from that image id; or attach a Volume / DurableDisk for files that must survive
persist_scope.note: Beam VMs (vm modes) keep the whole root disk (50 GiB default, max 100 GiB) across stop/start: persist_scope = whole there. No snapshot retention period is published.

locations_quote: Customer workloads run in the United States unless you choose a specific region or compute pool where the platform offers one.
